verdict: Yes. Our main final is the kind of file Cyrus describes. All of our files are built on the public x138 notebook. Of the +0.006 that exp87a gains on the public board over x138 (0.953 -> 0.959), about +0.004 (cap 6 +0.002, K +0.002) was chosen only from public reads, and our own lab disagreed or could not test it. About +0.001 (DaughterNet insertion) has an honest out-of-fold check. The last +0.001 (CI) has only an in-sample lab check plus three public reads. The finals pair limits the damage: partner #37 = x138 + insertion cap 4 carries none of cap 6, K or CI. So the realistic floor is roughly x138-level + insertion, not a collapse. The silver-level position (#141 now; silver cutoff around #199) is what is really at risk.

points.claim: The public gain decomposes step by step: x138 0.953 -> +insertion cap 4 0.954 (+0.001) -> cap 6 0.956 (+0.002) -> +K 0.958 (+0.002) -> +CI 0.959 (+0.001). Each display is rounded to 3 decimals, so each step is +-0.001. By how each piece was chosen, about 67% of the lift (+0.004) is public-tuned, about 17% (+0.001) is CV-backed and about 17% (+0.001) is mixed (in-sample lab + public reads).

x138 itself was never tested by us on unseen data. Its detector and edge network (pilkwang weights) saw all 199 train videos, so every lab we have on it is in-sample. The only honest check touches the V1284 coordinate head: heads trained on one embryo and tested on the other still beat no head. x138's relink/readmit/gap-filler chain comes from public notebooks and was tuned on the public board. However, about 407 teams sit exactly at 0.953, and most rows from 0.953 to 0.959 are x138 forks, so a drop of x138 itself is shared by everyone. What moves ranks is the tweaks on top of it.

points.claim: The edge filter already showed on our own project how in-sample labs inflate results. It passed the lab (+0.0162 and +0.0095) and gave 0 on the public board (0.947 and 0.946). Other teams saw the same pattern (Civitasmass, You WeiLin, sghwr in 744273). The lesson cuts both ways. We do not overrate the lab (cap 6 was not picked from it), but cap 6 and K are the reverse case: public gains without independent confirmation, and they can vanish on the private board the same way.

The public board may be a single embryo (about 29% of the test). All of our roughly 22 probes on the x138 base read that one embryo, and levers were kept or dropped by those reads. That is selection on one embryo, so the kept levers are biased upward. An unconfirmed claim (Satwik) says the public embryo has few divisions, which would make cap 6 and K, both division-side, the least reliable to carry over.
